title: A-Ch-D
hookLine: echad, one, as in the Shema

cards: The first chapter of Genesis counts the days of creation. Day two, a second day. Day three, a third.
But the first one isn't called the first. In the Hebrew, after the light and the dark, the verse says: "And there was evening and there was morning, one day." Not first.
One. The commentator Rashi noticed it and gave a reason: on that day God was alone, the only one in the world. Ordinal numbers come later.
On day one there is only one.

teach.h: THE LAST WORD OF THE SHEMA.

teach.b: Echad: one. First, the Shema, the line said morning and night, and at the end of a life: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." Echad is its last word.
The Talmud says that whoever draws out the word echad has their days drawn out.
So the custom is to linger on it, especially the last letter, and in that pause to let God's oneness fill everything: heaven, earth, and the four directions. Second, people.
In Genesis, a couple becomes basar echad, one flesh. At Sinai, a teaching of the rabbis says, the people camped facing the mountain like one person with one heart. Echad isn't only a number.
It's the word for many becoming whole. Third, this week. It began with G-D-L, great and growing.
Then K-T-N, the small one in the field. S-M-Ch, joy with a guest list. A-V-L, the mourner, and friends who sat in silence.
Sh-K-N, the presence that dwells with the neighbors. K-H-L, the crowd gathered to hear.

teach.h: THE WEEK: GREAT, SMALL, JOY, GRIEF, NEIGHBOR, CROWD.
teach.b: Great and small, joy and grief, neighbor and crowd.
The same Shema is said on a wedding morning and in a shiva house, by the tallest and the smallest voice in the room. One isn't the opposite of many. One is what many can become.

how: Jews say the Shema morning and evening, traditionally covering the eyes for the first line and lingering on its last word, echad, with the intention that God is one.

games.q: you're writing Genesis 1. day two is 'a second day', day three 'a third day'. what do you call day one?
games.why: the Hebrew says yom echad, one day. Rashi's reason: on that day there was only one, God alone.

practice: For a few minutes, choose one thing only, your breath, the sounds of the room or the feel of your hands, and when a second thing starts, a list, a worry, a plan, notice it and come back to the one, no scolding.
If you pray, you can say the Shema slowly and stay a while on its last word, the way the custom lingers on echad; if you don't, simply breathe out long on the word one.

wordCard.voice: A-Ch-D. Alef, chet, dalet: the root of echad, one, the last word of the Shema, and the first day of creation. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: one, the last word of the Shema, from the root alef, chet, dalet.

carryVoice: Your line: one. Great and small, joy and grief, all held in a single sentence. That's the week, done.
